macros.name: addtobeamertemplate
macros.doc: This command adds the ⟨pre-text⟩ before the text that is currently installed as the template ⟨element name⟩ and the ⟨post-text⟩ after it.

macros.name: alert
macros.doc: beamer offers the command \alert, which is used like \emph and, by default, typesets its argument in bright red.

macros.name: alt
macros.doc: The default text is shown on the specified slides, otherwise the alternative text.

macros.name: animatevalue
macros.doc: The ⟨name⟩ must be the name of a counter or a dimension. It will be varied between two values.

macros.name: AtBeginSection
macros.doc: The given text will be inserted at the beginning of every section.

macros.name: AtBeginSubsection
macros.doc: The given text will be inserted at the beginning of every subsection.

macros.name: beameroriginal
macros.doc: Inside ⟨text⟩, you can still access to original definitions using the command \beameroriginal, see the example.

macros.name: expandbeamertemplate
macros.doc: This command does the same as \usebeamertemplate{⟨beamer template name⟩}. The difference is that this command performs a direct expansion and does not scan for a star.

macros.name: ifbeamertemplateempty
macros.doc: This command checks whether a template is defined and set to a non-empty text.

macros.name: insertaspectratio
macros.doc: The user can access the aspect ratio of the presentation via the \insertaspectratio macro.

macros.name: insertnavigation
macros.doc: Some themes use the \insertnavigation to insert a navigation bar into the headline.

macros.name: insertshortframetitle
macros.doc: The ⟨short frame title⟩ is normally not shown, but it’s available via the \insertshortframetitle command.

macros.name: insertshortsubtitle
macros.doc: The ⟨short subtitle⟩ is not used by default, but is available via the insert \insertshortsubtitle.

macros.name: only
macros.doc: The command \only, which is introduced by beamer, normally simply inserts its parameter into the current frame. However, if an overlay specification is present, it “throws away” its parameter on slides that are not mentioned.

macros.name: opaqueness
macros.doc: The ⟨overlay specification⟩ specifies on which slides covered text should have which ⟨percentage of opaqueness⟩.

macros.name: pause
macros.doc: This command causes the text following it to be shown only from the next slide on, or, if the optional ⟨number⟩ is given, from the slide with the number ⟨number⟩.

macros.name: tableofcontents
macros.doc: Inserts a table of contents into the current frame.

macros.name: uncover
macros.doc: If the ⟨overlay specification⟩ is present, the ⟨text⟩ is shown (“uncovered”) only on the specified slides. On other slides, the text still occupies space and it is still typeset, but it is not shown or only shown as if transparent.

envs.name: columns
envs.doc: Inside this environment, \column commands create new columns.

envs.name: overlayarea
envs.doc: Everything within the environment will be placed in a rectangular area of the specified size. The area will have the same size on all slides of a frame, regardless of its actual contents.

envs.name: overprint
envs.doc: Inside the environment, use \onslide commands to specify different things that should be shown for this environment on different slides.

envs.name: quotation
envs.doc: The difference between a quotation and a quote is that the first has paragraph indentation, whereas the second hasn’t.

envs.name: thebibliography
envs.doc: Inserts a bibliography into the current frame.

classes/beamer#class-beamer:beameroption.key: second mode text on second screen
